entries.title: Terminal-only mean bias controls a geodesic norm detour
entries.statement: Let T be an integrable, translation-invariant undirected lattice FPP metric, h(x)=E T(0,x), and g a norm with g(x)=lim_m h(mx)/m on lattice x. Write b(x)=h(x)-g(x) and X(x,y)=T(x,y)-h(y-x). Then b(x)>=0. If z lies on any attained minimizing path from 0 to v, then g(z)+g(v-z)-g(v)=b(v)-b(z)-b(v-z)+X(0,v)-X(0,z)-X(z,v) <= b(v)+X(0,v)-X(0,z)-X(z,v). In particular, if the three centered errors have magnitude at most s, the detour is at most b(v)+3s. No upper bound on the two interior mean biases is required.
entries.proof_text:
nonnegative mean bias

For every lattice x, b(x):=h(x)-g(x)>=0. Indeed h(mx)<=m h(x) by the triangle inequality and translation invariance; divide by m and take the defining limit. This uses neither independence of selected paths nor conditional-product estimates.

terminal-bias detour identity

Write X(x,y)=T(x,y)-h(y-x). If z belongs to ANY minimizing path from 0 to v, additivity on that path gives exactly

g(z)+g(v-z)-g(v) = b(v)-b(z)-b(v-z)+X(0,v)-X(0,z)-X(z,v).

Consequently the left side is at most b(v)+X(0,v)-X(0,z)-X(z,v), and at most b(v)+3s whenever the three centered errors have magnitude at most s. No upper bound on b(z) or b(v-z) is needed. All endpoints will be bounded on a deterministic set before taking a union bound; z is not treated as an independent or fixed random endpoint.
assumptions: Translation invariance of the edge law
A limiting norm g with the stated expectation limit
An attained minimizing path contains z

entries.title: Euclidean detour inequality measures distance to a segment
entries.statement: For any d>=1, v in R^d with v!=0, and z in R^d, put L=|v|, S=|z|+|v-z| and r=dist(z,[0,v]) in Euclidean norm. Then S-L>=2r^2/S. The inequality includes projections of z beyond either endpoint.
entries.proof_text:
Euclidean detour inequality, including overshoot

For v!=0 let L=|v|, S=|z|+|v-z| and r=dist(z,[0,v]). Then S-L>=2r^2/S. Proof: if the projection of z onto the line through v lies in the segment, write its coordinate as t in [0,L] and perpendicular distance r. Convexity of t -> sqrt(t^2+r^2)+sqrt((L-t)^2+r^2) gives S>=sqrt(L^2+4r^2), hence S-L>=4r^2/(S+L)>=2r^2/S. If the projection lies outside the segment, r is the distance to the closer endpoint, the distance to the other endpoint is at least r, and S-L>=r. Thus S>=2r and the claimed bound follows. The case r=0 is immediate.

entries.title: A norm has a lower sphere-contact direction, with bounded lattice-rounding defect
entries.statement: Let g be a norm on R^d with g(x)<=b||x||_1, b>0. Let rho=min_{|u|=1}g(u)>0 and choose a minimizing unit u. Then g(x)>=rho|x| for all x and g(u)=rho. For integer n>=sqrt(d), round coordinates of nu to obtain v_n in Z^d. If delta=sqrt(d)/2 and K0=bd/2+rho delta, then v_n!=0, |v_n-nu|<=delta, and 0<=g(v_n)-rho|v_n|<=K0. This supplies a lower detour direction and no upper-curvature assertion.
entries.proof_text: Compactness of the Euclidean unit sphere gives u and rho. Homogeneity gives g(x)>=rho|x|. Coordinate rounding has Euclidean error <=sqrt(d)/2 and l1 error <=d/2. Thus g(v_n)<=rho n+bd/2 and |v_n|>=n-sqrt(d)/2, giving the upper defect bound. The lower defect bound follows from the global norm bound.
assumptions: A positive norm g on a finite-dimensional real vector space

entries.title: Finite-scale wandering tail from centered concentration and terminal mean bias
entries.statement: Consider iid edge FPP on Z^d, d>=2, with a<=tau_e<=b almost surely, 0<a<b<infinity. Let h(x)=E T(0,x), g its limiting norm, rho=min_{|u|=1}g(u), and u any minimizer. For integer n>=sqrt(d), round nu to v_n and put L_n=|v_n|, C=(b/a)sqrt(d), K0=bd/2+rho sqrt(d)/2, B_n=h(v_n)-g(v_n), Lambda_n={z in Z^d:||z||_1<=(b/a)||v_n||_1}, and A_n=2|Lambda_n|+1. Let D(0,v_n) be the maximum distance of all minimizing paths to the segment [0,v_n]. Suppose q>=0, alpha>0, K>=1 and E exp(alpha |T(0,w)-h(w)|/|w|^q)<=K for every nonzero lattice w. Then for s>=0, P(D(0,v_n)>sqrt(C L_n (B_n+K0+3s)/(2rho))) <= min(1,A_n K exp(-alpha s/(((C+1)L_n)^q))). If B_n<=H n^q log(2+n), choosing s=(((C+1)L_n)^q/alpha) log(A_n K n^p) gives probability <=n^(-p) and a threshold O(n^((1+q)/2)sqrt(log n)) for any fixed p>0. No independence of the centered passage times is used; this is an upper bound along one rounded direction and does not assert matched global exponents.
entries.proof_text:
a lower curvature direction exists for every norm

Let rho=min_{|u|=1} g(u)>0 and choose a minimizing unit vector u. Then g(x)>=rho|x| for every x and g(u)=rho, by compactness and homogeneity. Equivalently the g-unit ball is contained in a Euclidean sphere tangent in direction u. This supplies a lower quadratic detour in that direction; it supplies no UPPER curvature bound, no explicit direction, and no exponent existence.

For integer n>=sqrt(d), choose v_n by rounding each coordinate of n u to a nearest integer. Put delta=sqrt(d)/2, K0=bd/2+rho delta, and L_n=|v_n|. Then |v_n-nu|<=delta, L_n>=n-delta>0, and

0 <= g(v_n)-rho L_n <= K0.

The upper bound uses g(v_n)<=ng(u)+g(v_n-nu)<=rho n+bd/2. This handles a minimizing direction that is irrational; no rational direction is assumed to attain the sphere contact.

Every minimizing path to v_n has at most (b/a)||v_n||_1 edges, since its time is at most b||v_n||_1 and each edge costs at least a. Minimizers exist: loops strictly increase time and only finitely many paths can meet this length bound. With C=(b/a)sqrt(d), any vertex z on such a path has S<=C L_n. L3 and the norm bound therefore give

g(z)+g(v_n-z)-g(v_n) >= (2rho/C) dist(z,[0,v_n])^2/L_n - K0.

This bound applies simultaneously to all minimizing paths, including vertices whose projection overshoots either endpoint.

finite-scale tail from a centered envelope and one terminal bias

Assume q>=0, alpha>0 and K>=1 satisfy, for every nonzero lattice w,

E exp(alpha |T(0,w)-h(w)| / |w|^q) <= K.

This is an extra input, not an estimate proved here for q=1/3. Let B_n=h(v_n)-g(v_n). Define the deterministic set Lambda_n={z in Z^d: ||z||_1<=(b/a)||v_n||_1}, and A_n=2|Lambda_n|+1. All path vertices lie in Lambda_n. For z in Lambda_n both |z| and |v_n-z| are at most (C+1)L_n. Translation invariance, exponential Markov, and a finite union bound give, for s>=0,

P(max{|X(0,v_n)|, |X(0,z)|, |X(z,v_n)|:z in Lambda_n}>s)
 <= A_n K exp(-alpha s/(((C+1)L_n)^q)).

Zero-displacement terms are identically zero and omitted from the moment hypothesis. There is NO independence assumption between these variables.

Combining L2 and L4 proves the finite-scale implication

P(D(0,v_n)>sqrt(C L_n (B_n+K0+3s)/(2rho)))
 <= min(1, A_n K exp(-alpha s/(((C+1)L_n)^q))).

The maximum over all minimizing paths causes no extra factor: all their vertices already belong to the same deterministic Lambda_n.

For any p>0 set s=(((C+1)L_n)^q/alpha) log(A_n K n^p). The right side is n^(-p). If B_n<=H n^q log(2+n), then D(0,v_n)=O(n^((1+q)/2) sqrt(log n)) with this polynomial tail, for any fixed p. This is an upper bound along the rounded support direction, not equality of global exponents or a lower bound on wandering.
assumptions: The stated uniform centered exponential-moment input
For the final asymptotic consequence, the stated terminal mean-bias bound

entries.title: Rejected generic shortcut from centered concentration to nonrandom error
entries.statement: REJECTED INFERENCE: abstract subadditivity of h(n)=E T_n and a centered exponential concentration envelope alone do not imply h(n)-n lim_m h(m)/m=O(n^q log n) on that envelope scale. An FPP subadditive approximation theorem requires its additional stochastic and geometric hypotheses. This concept records a failed shortcut, not a theorem asserting the shortcut.
assumptions: The rejected statement concerns arbitrary subadditive sequences, not a proved iid FPP representation

entries.title: Deterministic subadditive countermodel has perfect centered concentration and large bias
entries.statement: Fix 0<beta<1. Put h(0)=0, h(n)=n+n^beta for integers n>=1, and T_n=h(n) deterministically. Then h is subadditive, lim_m h(m)/m=1, and E exp(alpha |T_n-E T_n|/n^q)=1 for every n>=1, alpha>0 and q>=0. Nevertheless h(n)-n=n^beta is not O(n^q log n) for q<beta. This is a counterexample to a generic inference, not an iid lattice FPP law.
entries.proof_text:
a refuted generic shortcut about the mean bias

Centered concentration plus abstract subadditivity alone cannot give the terminal bound. For 0<beta<1 let h(n)=n+n^beta for n>=1, h(0)=0, and T_n=h(n) deterministically. The concavity power inequality gives h(m+n)<=h(m)+h(n). The limiting slope is 1 and the centered variables vanish, so every centered exponential bound holds even with q=0. Yet h(n)-n=n^beta, which is not O(n^q log n) for q<beta. This is a countermodel to the GENERIC inference, not an iid lattice FPP example. Alexander's theorem has additional stochastic/geometric structure; that structure cannot be erased from a proof citation.
assumptions: Deterministic sequence rather than an FPP metric

entries.title: Rejected reuse of a lower-curvature direction as an upper-curvature direction
entries.statement: REJECTED INFERENCE: a norm satisfying a lower quadratic transverse bound at a supporting outer-sphere direction need not satisfy an upper quadratic transverse bound at that same direction. The direction in a lower-bound argument cannot be reused in an upper-bound argument without verifying the upper hypothesis.
assumptions: This is a rejected implication about arbitrary norms

entries.title: The l1 norm separates lower from upper quadratic curvature
entries.statement: For g(s,t)=|s|+|t| on R^2 and u=(1,0), u minimizes g on the Euclidean unit circle. For |t|<=1, g(u+(0,t))-g(u)=|t|>=t^2. There is no finite C such that g(u+(0,t))-g(u)<=C t^2 for every sufficiently small nonzero t, since the ratio is 1/|t|. This norm example makes no assertion about the limit shape of any particular iid FPP law.
entries.proof_text:
the lower curvature direction cannot be reused as an upper curvature direction

For g(s,t)=|s|+|t|, u=(1,0) minimizes g on the Euclidean unit circle and g(u)=1. For |t|<=1, g(u+(0,t))-g(u)=|t|>=t^2. But the ratio to t^2 is 1/|t|, unbounded as t tends to zero. Thus a supporting outer sphere giving a lower quadratic bound does not give an upper quadratic bound at the SAME direction. This norm example refutes that geometric substitution; it is not asserted to be the shape of Uniform[1,2] FPP.

entries.title: Primary-source clarification for the conditional KPZ theorem, pending Claude review
entries.statement: PRIMARY-SOURCE CHECK, review pending: Chatterjee, Annals of Mathematics 177 (2013), Theorem 1.1, states iid lattice weights, a nearly-Gamma law, a moment generating function near zero, the uniform upper/lower exponent definitions, and the matching conditions chi_a=chi_b and xi_a=xi_b for the relation chi=2xi-1. Its complete hypothesis list does not include a separate uniform-positive-curvature assumption. Proposition 5.1 provides suitable sphere-contact directions. This resolves an unknown-curvature flag in the retrieved secondary brain card only after source review; it supplies no matched-exponent proof for Uniform[1,2] and no current-openness certificate.
assumptions: Historical statement: the original 2013 theorem, not every subsequent theorem

relations.rationale: The terminal-bias identity controls the norm excess on every minimizing path; its two interior mean biases are nonnegative.
The segment-distance bound includes longitudinal overshoot and turns a geometric detour into a quadratic cost.
The selected norm direction and bounded rounding defect supply the quadratic norm lower bound without asserting uniform curvature.
The deterministic subadditive sequence has centered concentration on every scale but a mean bias n^beta.
The l1 norm has a lower quadratic bound at the selected direction and an unbounded ratio to any upper quadratic bound there.
A conditional passage-time-to-wandering bridge useful for P0110; neither exponent matching nor a solution of the target is proved.
Clarifies the conditional theorem hypotheses for the P0110 target while retaining the unresolved matching-exponent gap.
